problems.stem: A facilitator note reads: "The AI essay tool is engaging and saves grading time, so adopt it." On a Design Tension Studio map, what is the strongest objection?
options: The note should also mention how much money the tool costs.
The note names only the benefit axis (speed) and leaves the competing value, student authorship and teacher judgment, off the map.
The note is too short to be a real facilitator note.
The note should have been written by the AI tool itself.
problems.explanation: A Design Tension Studio map has to show both axes of the conflict. Naming only the benefit hides the value being traded away.

problems.stem: A team decides an AI tool may draft essay comments. Which line turns that preference into a negotiated decision a mentor teacher could later audit?
options: The team agreed the tool was a good idea.
Everyone liked the tool, so we will use it this unit.
AI drafts comments, but the teacher reads and signs each one before release, with a mandatory human first pass on flagged-for-support students.
We will see how it goes and decide later.
problems.explanation: A negotiated decision states a commitment the team can be held to and later test, not just that they liked the tool.

problems.stem: When mapping the equity risk of the AI essay tool, what does a defensible facilitator note do?
options: States the tool carries the same risk for every student equally.
Names the specific students most likely to be misread (ELL students, students with IEPs) so the equity cost is located, not averaged.
Leaves equity out because the tool is only a draft assistant.
Assumes the vendor already handled fairness.
problems.explanation: Equity risk lands unevenly. A defensible note locates who bears it rather than treating the class as one undifferentiated group.

problems.stem: A facilitator justifies adopting the tool entirely on the grounds that "students find it fun." Why is this not yet a defensible decision on the tension map?
options: Fun is the only thing that matters in a classroom decision.
Engagement alone is not a justification; the note must tie the choice to a protected learning value and a named risk.
The decision is fine as long as test scores are not mentioned.
The note simply needs to be longer to be defensible.
problems.explanation: Engagement matters but does not replace evidence about learning, access, or risk. The map must connect the choice to a protected value and a named cost.
